dialogues.speaker: Rhythmos
dialogues.text: Hmm, the sound of the ball hitting the target is nice and crisp. If we can work it into a steady rhythm, it'd make the perfect accompanying beat!

choices.text: I'd like to play a round of Rhythm Ball!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Alright, I'm looking forward to your performance. Get out there and give 'em a show!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Hey there, and welcome to our game!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: I'm a musician hired by Master Xilonen to run this Dance-Off Stage.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Master"?

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Yeah! Whether it's the technology that goes into designing, building, and maintaining our equipment, or the ability to DJ, Xilonen's the master that all us musicians aspire to be!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: When she's DJ-ing, she flows freely between dozens of styles and techniques. Simply put, she can handle any style, with style!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: And her sense of hearing is, like, razor-sharp!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Whenever part of a song's too dry, whenever there's a pitch deviation of more than half a semitone, or whenever the sound effects have been pushed just a bit too far — Master Xilonen can tell, even with her ears stuffed full of Quenepa Berries!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why would she stuff her ears with...

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Quenepa Berries? Because they're full of juice, and listening through them's like being stuck underwater. It's the toughest of trials for any musician around!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Although Master Xilonen didn't mention it, I feel like sharp hearing's also helpful for warriors and adventurers.

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: If you wanna sharpen your ears, pay Master Xilonen a visit!

response.speaker: Rhythmos
response.text: Any time's a good time! Don't be shy about saying hi if you see any of our DJs putting on a show!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Yo, {NICKNAME}, don't you look full of energy!

choices.text: What kind of songs do you like, Mualani?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Me? I'm fine with pretty much anything!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Relaxing melodies, heart-pumping beats, jaunty tunes — I love 'em all!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Ah, but I'm not great at rocking out to music that's a bit more solemn and formal... I don't listen to such songs often, but I don't dislike them, either!

choices.text: Do you have any advice for the game?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hmm, let me jog the ol' noggin...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Based on my experience playing beach volleyball, I think it's easy to slip up if you get anxious.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Sometimes, when I see the ball flying at me, I freeze up thinking of all the ways I can hit it back!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: So don't sweat the small stuff. Just go with the flow, y'know?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Makes sense. I'll give it a try!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Of course, you can't rely solely on your intuition for contests of strategy, or when things get serious. You gotta look before you leap, too!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Everything in moderation!

choices.text: Great game. I wanna go again!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Look at you go! With your skills and a little more practice, you'll set some unbeatable records in no time — I know it!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #Looking good, {NICKNAME}! You're well on your way to becoming an improv master, I'd say.

choices.text: Do you have any tips, Xilonen?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Do I ever. Seems like you're interested in the nitty-gritty of DJ-ing, huh?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, then. First up, a good DJ knows their equipment.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I've collected a number of schematics from making lots of music equipment in the past. Feel free to pick 'em up next time you swing by.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Learning theory's always the blandest part of picking up new music techniques. But once you nail the basics, you'll improve by leaps and bounds.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm expecting great things from you, alright?

choices.text: Xilonen, what style of music's your favorite?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: My favorite style...? Hmm, hard to say.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Way I see it, the overall production quality of a song's the most important...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The melody's flow, the arrangement of the piece, the instruments chosen, the recording quality, and overall processing... They've all got standards to meet.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Mainstream styles sometimes produce pieces with exceptional musicality. Conversely, seemingly sophisticated niche styles might churn out less-than-ideal work.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And fooling your audience with a sloppy piece of music by simply slapping a "niche" label on seems... I don't know, rather base?

choices.text: Yeah, you can't just fake it and hope to make it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #In short, there are no shortcuts when it comes to learning music theory, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The basics are the most important. I'm sure you'll study hard, though.

choices.text: Maybe it's best to ignore the labels...
I'll keep looking for inspiration, then.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If you've got any good ideas, feel free to just hum 'em for me. I'll jot them down.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Mmm... I can feel the warmth of your emotions from how much you enjoyed the game. Heehee. I'm sure you'll have sweet, relaxing dreams tonight.

choices.text: Do you also listen to fast-paced music, Mizuki?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: That's a... classic line of questioning.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Well, I'll listen to whatever my friends recommend, even if it's not to my tastes. I wouldn't want to let them down, after all.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I can enjoy lively music, but I prefer soothing, elegant tunes. I can't say I particularly care for instrumental variety or technical sophistication.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: As long as the melody is pleasing to the ears, even if it's a cappella or a slow solo, they won't feel bland to me. Rather, I find they exude a sense of beautiful serenity.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Well... next time you find yourself a free moment, how about I show you some of my favorites? I can brew some tea, prepare some snacks... And we can take our time enjoying them.

choices.text: Maybe give some new styles a chance?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Why not? With your tastes, I'm sure you can show me some hidden gems outside of my usual wheelhouse. If you've got a free moment, don't be shy, okay?

choices.text: I want to see you give the game a try.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I sure could... but that might be flouting the rules.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: As one of the designers, I know the ins and outs of every stage. It might be a little boring for you to watch.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Games work best with the element of surprise, and designers should think outside the box to create that. Becoming predictable is the mark of bad development.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Of course, drawing outside the box is your field of expertise.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I do hope you can take part in game development and planning in the future. I'd love to play something you designed~

choices.text: Hope you rest well too, Mizuki.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Don't worry. Inviting you here makes this event a success in my book. I'm sure my sleep tonight will be thrice as restful as usual~

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like the DJ is immersed in the music. Let's go ask Mualani and the others about the situation first...)
